payload.textAr: A rejection and a denial are not the same thing
payload.textEn: A rejection and a denial are not the same thing

payload.mdAr:
The words are used interchangeably in conversation and mean different things in practice. A **rejection** happens before the payer assesses the claim: something about its form or its data stopped it from being processed at all. A **denial** happens after assessment: the payer read the claim and decided not to pay.

The distinction is not pedantry. It decides what you do next. A rejection is corrected and resubmitted. A denial is a decision, and changing a decision means either fixing what it was based on or arguing against it.
payload.mdEn:
The words are used interchangeably in conversation and mean different things in practice. A **rejection** happens before the payer assesses the claim: something about its form or its data stopped it from being processed at all. A **denial** happens after assessment: the payer read the claim and decided not to pay.

The distinction is not pedantry. It decides what you do next. A rejection is corrected and resubmitted. A denial is a decision, and changing a decision means either fixing what it was based on or arguing against it.

payload.defAr: The claim was not processed. Usually a format or data failure, often caught before it reaches the payer at all. Corrected and resubmitted, it is treated as a new claim rather than a disputed one.
payload.defEn: The claim was not processed. Usually a format or data failure, often caught before it reaches the payer at all. Corrected and resubmitted, it is treated as a new claim rather than a disputed one.

payload.defAr: The claim was processed and payment was refused. The reason may be about coverage, documentation, timing, or authorisation, and the route back is correction or appeal depending on which.
payload.defEn: The claim was processed and payment was refused. The reason may be about coverage, documentation, timing, or authorisation, and the route back is correction or appeal depending on which.
payload.exampleAr: Training example: a claim refused because the service preceded the policy effective date is a denial — it was read and judged, not bounced.
payload.exampleEn: Training example: a claim refused because the service preceded the policy effective date is a denial — it was read and judged, not bounced.

payload.mdAr: Classify before you act. The most expensive mistake in denial work is appealing something that should have been corrected and resubmitted: appeals are slow, they consume the filing window, and a denial that was really a data error will lose an appeal it never needed to enter.
payload.mdEn: Classify before you act. The most expensive mistake in denial work is appealing something that should have been corrected and resubmitted: appeals are slow, they consume the filing window, and a denial that was really a data error will lose an appeal it never needed to enter.

itemsAr: A rejection was never assessed; a denial was assessed and refused.
The root cause, not the wording of the notice, decides the correct action.
Correct the claim to match the record — never the record to match the claim.
Appealing what should have been corrected wastes the filing window and usually loses.

payload.promptAr: A claim comes back refused. The payer assessed it and says the service required permission that was never obtained.
payload.promptEn: A claim comes back refused. The payer assessed it and says the service required permission that was never obtained.

steps.showAr: Was it assessed? Yes — the payer read it and refused payment.
steps.showEn: Was it assessed? Yes — the payer read it and refused payment.
steps.whyAr: That makes it a denial, not a rejection. A rejection was never processed at all.
steps.whyEn: That makes it a denial, not a rejection. A rejection was never processed at all.

steps.whyAr: The root cause, not the wording of the notice, decides the action.
steps.whyEn: The root cause, not the wording of the notice, decides the action.

steps.showAr: Check whether permission existed at the time of service: it did not.
steps.showEn: Check whether permission existed at the time of service: it did not.
steps.whyAr: For an authorisation denial, an appeal only succeeds if the permission existed.
steps.whyEn: For an authorisation denial, an appeal only succeeds if the permission existed.

steps.showAr: Decide: do not appeal. Absorb the loss or bill according to the policy.
steps.showEn: Decide: do not appeal. Absorb the loss or bill according to the policy.
steps.whyAr: An appeal without the permission loses, and it uses up the filing window on the way.
steps.whyEn: An appeal without the permission loses, and it uses up the filing window on the way.

payload.answerAr: No appeal. Classifying first is what stops a hopeless appeal from being filed.
payload.answerEn: No appeal. Classifying first is what stops a hopeless appeal from being filed.

payload.situationAr: A claim comes back within hours with a message that a required field was blank. It never reached assessment. A colleague has already started drafting an appeal.
payload.situationEn: A claim comes back within hours with a message that a required field was blank. It never reached assessment. A colleague has already started drafting an appeal.

decisions.optionAr: Let the appeal go ahead — a refusal is a refusal.
decisions.optionEn: Let the appeal go ahead — a refusal is a refusal.
decisions.consequenceAr: There is no decision to appeal. The appeal is slow, consumes the filing window, and will lose an argument it never needed to enter.
decisions.consequenceEn: There is no decision to appeal. The appeal is slow, consumes the filing window, and will lose an argument it never needed to enter.

decisions.optionAr: Stop the appeal, correct the blank field, and resubmit.
decisions.optionEn: Stop the appeal, correct the blank field, and resubmit.
decisions.consequenceAr: It is a rejection: corrected and resubmitted, it is treated as a new claim rather than a disputed one. Hours, not weeks.
decisions.consequenceEn: It is a rejection: corrected and resubmitted, it is treated as a new claim rather than a disputed one. Hours, not weeks.

decisions.optionAr: Call the payer to dispute the refusal.
decisions.optionEn: Call the payer to dispute the refusal.
decisions.consequenceAr: The payer will confirm the claim was never processed. There is nothing to dispute until it is resubmitted.
decisions.consequenceEn: The payer will confirm the claim was never processed. There is nothing to dispute until it is resubmitted.
